newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania posts higher interest income.
newsitem.headline: Christiania posts higher interest income.

text.p: Norway's second largest bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA said on Wednesday net interest income rose 3.6 percent in the first nine months despite continued pressure on interest rate margins from tough competition.
The bank posted net interest income of 2.56 billion crowns in the period to September 30 compared with 2.47 billion crowns a year ago.
Operating profit before loan losses grew 11.4 percent to 1.40 billion crowns against 1.26 billion crowns as net profit fell 33 percent to 1.55 billion crowns versus 2.32 billion.
Net profit in the nine-month 1995 period included a reduction in the general loan loss allowance of 750 million crowns, the bank said.

"It's gratifying to see that the group's net interest income has improved...and particularly to see that net commissions and fees have increased by 10.7 percent in the same period, considering the keen competition which we experience at present," Borger Lenth, Christiania's Preseident and Chief Executive Officer, said in a statement.

"Collectively, other non-interest income amounts to around 30 percent of the total income. The objective is to increase this income through iomproved sales of payment services, foreign exchandge, fund management and insurance products as well as advisory services."

The bank said rationalisation measures were proceeding as planned, and attributed a 3.7 percent increase in overall costs to 2.25 billion crowns in the period to consultancy fees related to rationalisation and the acquisition of Norgeskreditt bank.
"Consequently our costs have shown a development in line with expectations, and so far this year constitute 63 percent of our income (excluding gains on securities)," Lenth said.

For the third quarter operating profit before loan losses and profit on long-term securities amounted to 422 million crowns against 404 million crowns, while net profit slid 10 percent to 451 million crowns.
Third-quarter net interest income rose to 858 million crowns, compared with 791 million crowns, including a one-off item of 21 million crowns relating to a court ruling.
"Despite a continued pressure on interest rate margins, the net interest income has been maintained at a satisfactory level," Christiania said.
Provisions for loan losses and guarantees in the three-month period showed a net income of 26 million crowns.

The bank said loans to businesses and the retail market in Norway had shown very small new losses and several minor writebacks in the quarter. "In the longer term, the bank must expect a level of loan losses higher then what was the case in 1994/1995, and so far in 1996," it said.
